newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai sugar premiums steady, crush result awaited.
newsitem.headline: Thai sugar premiums steady, crush result awaited.

text.p: Thai sugar premiums were in the doldrums this week as the market monitored the progress of crushing before deciding to trade again, industry sources said on Wednesday.
Steady Thai sugar prices also resulted from a drop in world sugar prices, they said.
Premiums for raw sugar for January/March delivery were quoted at around 0.80/0.90 cents (bid/offer) a pound over New York futures, barely changed from a week earlier.
March/May and May/July deliveries remained unchanged at 0.45/0.55 cents over New York.

"Most exporters were committed until March. Some overseas buyers are now seeking to buy April and June delivery. But we would rather wait to see how the crushing goes before making a move," said one sugar mill manager.

"The activity in the market was also subdued because buyers were sidelined by idea that prices could fall further while exporters considered the current level already too low and are reluctant to sell below this level," said a trader with one Japanese trading firm.

Many in the industry were optimistic that the crushing would meet the Sugar Board target for 1996/97 (Nov-Oct) sugar cane production at 60.32 million tonnes and 6.28 million tonnes tel quel for sugar output.
Any possible impact of a crushing delay by some mills in the northeast was seen to be offset by the speeding up of crushing by several mills in the central region, industry sources said.
The molasses market was also quiet as sellers unhappy with the sliding prices stayed on the sidelines.
"Many mills in the northeast which delayed their crushing schedule did not feel the urgency to get rid of the stock," one molasses trader said.
The prices of molasses this week dipped to around $38-40 per tonne FOB Bangkok compared with $41-43 per tonne two weeks ago.
At ports, sugar vessel movement picked up after a long monsoon.
Vessel Orient Express I left Thai port on November 29 with 1,000 tonnes of white sugar for Cambodia.

The same vessel is scheduled to be at a Thai port again between December 5-8 and 19-22 to load 1,200 tonnes of white sugar each time for Cambodia. Tate and Lyle is said to be the buyer of both batches.
Vessel Parkarti Sembilan is expected to arrive here on December 28 to load 5,250 tonnes of raw sugar that Indonesia bought through Marubeni.
